blocks.text: With Katy Correa, D’Johé Kouadio, Samir Guesmi
Courtesy of The Party Film Sales
Languages French, Manjak, Wolof, Creole Portuguese With English subtitles

Moving between a memorial ritual in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in France, Dao brings these two rites of passage into intimate conversation, exploring diasporic lives shaped by distance, memory and belonging. Blending fictional narrative with interviews and rehearsal scenes with its performers, Gomis creates a warm, richly layered, jazz-inflected portrait in which lived experience and performance continually illuminate one another.

blocks.text: Cameroonian director Bernard Auguste Kouemo Yanghu’s outstanding feature debut is a poignant tale of an ageing parent who has been left behind.
Bertil Nilsson’s distinctive debut follows Robin as he moves through temporary jobs and tentative relationships in search of a place to belong.
Nolitha Refilwe Mkulisi’s debut feature – a tender love letter to Tapoleng, her hometown in South Africa – offers an intimate evocation of a community in transition.
